old_title: Arsenal v West Ham, Manchester City 1-3 Tottenham: WSL clockwatch - live
new_title: Arsenal 0-0 West Ham, Manchester City 1-3 Tottenham: WSL clockwatch - as it happened
old_text:
Some quotes from the Manchester City manager, Andree Jeglertz, following that shock defeat: "I think we struggled with their press in the first half and then in the second half they punished us on a couple of transitions. They ran through us too easily.
"We didn't create that many chances. We got a little bit stuck and they knew what we were doing. We didn't give the urgency I was hoping for. We've played a lot of games and I felt that in the second half we lacked a bit of energy.
"We played a very good team today and the title is far in Spring so we don't talk about that now. We talk about winning games, performing how we want to and that's what we didn't do today.
"We've a lot of games to play - great games and tough games - and we want to do better than this. I'm not concerned at all."
The Manchester City players looked stunned, dejected and a little bewildered, as they offer polite applause to their supporters who have stayed behind after the shock defeat. The home fans here had known nothing but home victories since Andrée Jeglertz took charge, but his 100% home league record has come to a crushing end here. They were second best and they will know it. Tottenham, on the other hand, as overjoyed as they celebrate in front of their fans on the far side. Are they in the Champions League race? Surely they are now.
Birmingham 1-1 Manchester United: Manchester United appeal for a penalty as Drury - who replaced Riviere - is fouled by McKenna on the edge of the box, but the referee gives a free kick instead. Replays show the challenge took place just outside. The correct decision from the ref.
GOAL! Manchester City 1-2 Tottenham (Matilda Vinberg, 74)
Vinberg gives Tottenham the lead!
Spence splits the City defence with a brilliant pass and Vinberg latches onto it before cutting the ball onto her left foot with a brilliant bit of skill and sliding a low shot into the net. A fantastic goal!
Birmingham 1-0 Manchester United: Birmingham still have the lead and Hurtré comes close to making it two. The striker brings down a pass and takes it into the box with her first touch. She gets past Lundkvist before shooting, but her attempt rolls jut past the post.
Manchester City 1-1 Tottenham: Incredibly, Manchester City have only had one shot on goal in the game so far. Spurs have been excellent since conceding.
new_text:
Here's Tom' Garry's roundup of the day's WSL action.
Arsenal remain winless at home in the WSL this season after being held to another frustrating draw at the Emirates, this time by West Ham. Arsenal had 22 shots at goal but were unable to break the deadlock, as their under-pressure head coach Renée Slegers oversaw a sixth home league draw out of six, leaving Arsenal eight points behind the top three.
Manchester United left it late to come from behind and beat Birmingham 2-1 but Simi Awujo's last-gasp header from a corner gave them a valuable win and extended Eva Olid's side's club-record unbeaten run to 14 matches in all competitions. Birmingham had led inside four minutes through Lee Geum-Min's expert volley but Elisabeth Terland's close-range finish with 10 minutes to go and Awujo's 94th-minute winner snatched it, moving Olid's fourth-placed team just six points off the top.
Elsewhere, the bottom side Charlton collected their first point of the season as they drew 1-1 with Aston Villa, while Brighton moved into the top half with a 1-0 victory at Everton, courtesy of Maz Pacheco's early own goal.
Kym Little spoke to the BBC: "We all take responsibility [for not winning]. They've all been tight games and performances where we've not hit our rhythm and found the net. It's something we work on relentlessly but it's just not coming off in matches. We need to go away, look at ourselves, keep working hard and together to make sure it comes in the next game.
"There are lots of elements across the board that we can work on and we review. We need to find our way to score, whatever they may be. We'll put everything into it to be better."
West Ham's Viviane Asseyi, who had a fine game, spoke to the BBC: "Really happy. It was really a team performance. We stayed collected, we stayed together. It was not easy but we stayed compact and played together. I'm very happy."
Just like the first half, it closes with a Maanum effort that offers no danger to the West Ham. A long punt forward from the Gunners keeper comes to nothing, and it's another failure to win at the Emirates. They won't have another chance to win at the Emirates in 2026, and the pressure is on Renee Slegers.
Into the last 10 minutes, with the traffic increasingly one-way, and Maanum forcing a corner. Olivia Smith goes down - penalty? That looked a shout but the referee gives a corner. Next, was there a handball from Nystrom? Again, waved away.
Foord cuts inside but runs into heavy traffic. West Ham are holding their line very well and are on course to see out their first ever point at Arsenal in the WSL.
Charles Antaki had this to say at half-time and it still stands: "Not a very encouraging half from Arsenal. Hard not to feel that the tide has gone out on this team, maybe taking the manager with it. Even if they win this one - which at the moment doesn't seem especially likely - they'll still be way off. Disappointing for all Arsenal fans, maybe be spoiled by the glories of previous iterations of the team. This one is not measuring up."
It's a first point of the season and the Addicks player look disappointed it wasn't more. They really pushed at the end for a first win. They feel that one got away. Gillian Kenney had a number of chances at the end.
The Gunners stepping it up, and so are their fans. From a corner West Ham are asked to clear the ball, and do so hurriedly. Arsenal look similarly jittery from a West Ham counter.
Two bites of the cherry for Caitlin Foord, the ball bouncing back out from her first chanc and then smashed back wide. Colin Firth, star of Fever Pitch, Mr Darcy himself, is in the crowd.
Frida Maanum's shot wide of the post was the last effort of another 45 minutes of home frustration at the Emirates. The response from home fans is tepid. It's just not happening for them. They have had 64% to 36% possession yet conceded four shots to nine.
Six minutes were added on after Lisa Baum was carried off. That incident does seem to have taken some of the steam from this contest. We await news of the youngster.
Some concern here as Lisa Baum, the Arsenal player, goes down, and with nobody around her. She is is receiving a great deal of treatment, all the medical team are on.
At last, some vigour from the Gunners, it taking Nystrom's clearance to avert danger for the Hammers. Alessia Russo has been dropping deep in search of the ball.
More concern for Renee Slegers on the bench. West Ham continue to look the more vigorous team, with Kym Little buying a foul when she is sluggish in possession.
It's half-time at St Helens, where it's still Everton 0-1 Brighton, via that Maz Pacheco own-goal, which was a terrible mix-up, a back-pass that was allowed to roll in.
At the Valley, it's still Charlton 1-0 Aston Villa at the break, following that Keira Flannery penalty after Akane Okuma's foul on Cassandra Korhonen.
The Hammers go close, Arsenal nervy as van Domselaar commits forward and makes a save as the ball comes in, and it takes a defender to clear the danger.
It's still Charlton 1-0 Aston Villa, and Everton 0-1 Brighton as half-time approaches in each match. Ashleigh Neville has just driven a shot wide for Charlton, the WSL veteran clearly fancied a crack.
